stories.Headline: IATA - IATA's 2026 Global Passenger Survey: Travelers Embrace Biometrics and AI but Entry Requirements Remain a Barrier
stories.Summary:
The International Air Transport Association released the results of its 2026 Global Passenger Survey on 28 October 2026, during its World Passenger Symposium in Macao. The survey found that biometrics are becoming mainstream, with 58% of passengers having experienced biometrics at some point in their airport journey in the past 12 months, up from 50% in 2025 and 24 percentage points higher than in 2022. Satisfaction with biometrics reached its highest level yet, with 87% of those who experienced it saying they were happy, up from 86% in 2025. The survey also found that 49% of travelers have used artificial intelligence for travel planning, and that immigration requirements discouraged 43% of passengers from visiting a destination, up from 33% in 2025.

The survey reports that 78% of travelers would be willing to share biometric information to skip showing a passport or boarding pass at checkpoints, and 75% of those prefer to register once in advance. It found that 84% are interested in using a digital passport for online check-in, 82% would share a digital passport with an airline at booking for personalized services such as visa information, and 82% are interested in a smartphone combining a digital wallet, digital passport and loyalty cards. Among AI users, 21% searched for flights to a specific destination, 19% looked for the cheapest flights and 17% sought inspiration for where to travel. On entry requirements, 53% of discouraged passengers said the process is too complex, while privacy and cost were each cited by 17%, and 86% are likely to share immigration information digitally before departure, up from 83% in 2025.

Nick Careen, IATA's Senior Vice President for Operations, Safety and Security, said passengers are embracing technology to make travel easier, with AI becoming a mainstream planning tool and biometrics and digital identity creating a faster airport experience. He said many travelers still face barriers from complex immigration and visa processes, and that governments can help by simplifying entry requirements, eliminating duplicate checks and accelerating the issuance and acceptance of secure digital travel credentials. He said passengers like biometrics and want more, and that to make biometrics the norm for international travel, governments must agree a framework for issuing and accepting secure digital passports, or Digital Travel Credentials. He also said passengers want to apply for visas online and complete immigration procedures before reaching the airport, and that although more than 100 countries issue eVisas, there is little consistency in how they are checked, so governments should adopt the tools that already exist.

The survey results are based on over 10,000 responses from more than 200 countries, and IATA represents over 370 airlines accounting for some 85% of global air traffic. Regionally, Asia-Pacific travelers reported the highest overall satisfaction at 90%, while European travelers reported the lowest at 84% and were the most cautious about digital travel technology. Middle East travelers were the most likely to use AI for travel planning at 72% and showed the strongest interest in digital passports at 91%, while North American travelers reported the highest biometric use at 63% but the strongest concern about data breaches. African travelers were the most likely to have been discouraged by immigration requirements at 52%, and Latin America and the Caribbean reported the largest improvement in overall satisfaction, up 5 points.

stories.Headline: Pflugerville adopts new policy for AI, surveillance technology and data privacy
stories.Summary:
The Pflugerville City Council unanimously approved a resolution on Tuesday establishing an oversight policy for artificial intelligence, surveillance technology and data sharing, according to the city. City Manager James Hartshorn said Council Member Jonathan Coffman proposed the Safe, Accountable, Fair and Explainable, or SAFE, technology policy. The policy sets standards for reviewing and approving technology that could affect residents' rights or access to city services, and it limits how the city can use and share data. The city's move came two months after the council unanimously voted to end its master services agreement with Flock Safety, which provided 28 automated license plate reader cameras. Officials said concerns about whether Flock could adequately protect data and comply with Pflugerville's privacy standards drove that decision.

Under the SAFE policy, the city will classify technology as low, moderate or high risk based on how it is used and its potential impacts. The city manager will keep authority over routine, administrative uses of technology, while high-risk systems, such as those used by law enforcement, will require City Council approval. The city must establish a technology oversight committee within 90 days to provide recommendations to staff and elected officials. Within 90 days, the city must also establish a technology review process, identify high-risk systems and data-sharing arrangements, and launch a transparency website. The policy restricts how the city and its vendors can use collected data, for example by preventing vendors from using it to train general-purpose AI models, and it restricts surveillance technologies and data-sharing without City Council approval.

Mayor Doug Weiss said technology helps the city serve its community better, but that should not come at the expense of privacy, accountability or public trust. He said residents deserve to know how these tools are used and what the city is doing to protect their information. Council Member Rudy Metayer called the policy a living document and encouraged residents to get involved as the city navigates implementing the SAFE standards. Coffman said he views the current policy as a stepping stone that sets the city up to keep protecting residents' data security and privacy as technology rapidly evolves. He said the city should want all employees to have access to the best tools to do their job, and it should also want a human in the loop making the final decision that will impact a resident.

The city will implement the remaining requirements next year, starting with the riskiest systems. The city's existing technology can continue to operate under its approved uses and current contract terms, but the policy requires additional review of those technologies and their safety when the council renews or significantly updates its contracts. The policy clarifies that AI and automated systems can aid city staff in their day-to-day work, but these systems should never replace human judgment, especially when decisions directly impact residents. The Austin City Council passed a similar resolution, called the TRUST Act, earlier this year.

stories.Headline: Media, privacy law
stories.Summary:
A new privacy law in India is set to take effect in May next year, and more than 20 news publishers have gone to court to challenge it. The publishers include top-ranking outlets and companies owned by Mukesh Ambani and Gautam Adani, such as Network18 and NDTV. They filed their challenge in the Supreme Court, and the court began hearing the case on Tuesday. The law was passed this year and is meant to protect the digital personal data of internet users, and it also covers platforms like Meta and Google.

The law requires journalists to get prior consent from any person they want to investigate, including a corrupt politician or bureaucrat. Publishers can be forced to erase such reports from their platforms immediately. The petitioners argue this amounts to pre-censorship, would trample investigative work, and could let the central government identify journalists' sources. They say it would turn investigative journalism into a benign and neutral recorder of events. The government had verbally promised to protect media freedom but would not commit to that assurance.

The IT minister, Vaishnaw, said journalistic freedom is guaranteed by the Constitution and there is no intention to affect it. He said he is inviting all editors and that the government is happy to take their suggestions on record and is open to acting accordingly if there is any doubt. The government has also invited media editors for consultations to clarify protections for journalistic sources. The Supreme Court has asked the government to respond to the lawsuit before November 17.

The case comes amid accusations that press freedom in India has declined since Narendra Modi took office in 2014. Critics say many mainstream outlets have not done enough to scrutinise his government, which says it respects press freedom. The article also cites Reporters Without Borders, which ranked India 157th among 180 countries for press freedom. It says media establishments face pressure from central investigation agencies and that many are not inclined to court trouble.

stories.Headline: Meta launches two new AI apps, including one aimed at kids
stories.Summary:
US Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Edward Markey of Massachusetts opened an inquiry into what they called serious privacy and safety risks around Meta's AI smart glasses. They sent a letter to Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg on October 30, 2026. The senators pointed to reports in 404 Media and the BBC about men secretly filming women with the glasses and posting the recordings to social media. They also cited reports and a lawsuit saying Meta's AI contractors reviewed eyewear footage of people undressing and engaging in sexual activity.

The letter asks Meta to answer questions about accidental camera activation and tampering with the recording indicator. It asks whether the glasses blur faces and license plates for some AI interactions, as Meta does on Facebook and Instagram. It asks when imagery becomes accessible to employees or contractors, and when it is used to train AI models. Citing Meta's own documents, it asks whether the company did detailed human rights due diligence and safety testing before release. The senators asked for answers by Thanksgiving, November 26, 2026.

Separately, ZDNET reported on October 27, 2026, that Meta's Muse AI assistant, launched September 8, had passed 10 million users, with about 25 percent using it daily, according to Meta's third-quarter earnings call. Meta said Muse can gather information about people who do not use it, for example when a user connects a calendar and asks about meetings, which can include attendees' names and event details. Meta said it cannot predict what information about a non-user may be included. Calli Schroeder of Epic.org said that without better protections Muse becomes a nightmare for people who choose not to engage with it, and privacy law expert Alexis Shore Ingber said platforms have a responsibility to protect people who do not consent to data collection by default.

The articles also note other complaints about the glasses, including recording without consent after a firmware update, use by ICE agents during raids, and surveillance concerns raised by the New York City Police counterterrorism unit in January 2026. California Governor Gavin Newsom vetoed a bill in October 2026 that would have banned secret recording with wearables in private areas of businesses. The senators told Zuckerberg that Meta's commitment to privacy rings hollow if the company cannot show meaningful steps to prevent its products from facilitating those harms. ZDNET reported that Meta is experimenting with AI making phone calls to businesses for Muse users, and that business owners can ask not to receive them.

stories.Headline: OpenAI suing to stop B.C. privacy commissioner's Tumbler Ridge investigation
stories.Summary:
OpenAI filed a lawsuit in B.C. on Monday seeking to stop an investigation by the province's privacy commissioner. The investigation concerns the connection between the Tumbler Ridge shooter's use of ChatGPT and the February school shooting. The Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner is seeking production of all of alleged shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar's ChatGPT logs. It also wants all documents related to the company's decision not to report the activity to police until after the shootings.

Van Rootselaar shot and killed eight people on Feb. 10 in Tumbler Ridge, before killing herself. The next day, OpenAI reported to the RCMP that the company had banned Van Rootselaar from ChatGPT for activity related to the shootings. At some stage, Van Rootselaar circumvented the ban and started a second account. OpenAI shut down the shooter's ChatGPT account in June 2025 after it was flagged for concerning behaviour, but the company did not notify police. The privacy office says it originally asked OpenAI for information after media reports linked ChatGPT with the killings, and the company did not comply.

The privacy office launched an investigation in June, followed by an order compelling production of the information last September, which the tech company is now challenging. Privacy commissioner Michael Harvey wants to know whether the use of personal information in the delivery of the service is one a reasonable person would consider appropriate in the circumstances, including the potential for responses to influence behaviour. OpenAI says it has turned over the chat logs to police, and argues the privacy commissioner has no coherent rationale for his investigation. OpenAI also denies breaching B.C.'s privacy rules in connection with the case. The company argues that the province's U.S. lawsuit alleges the opposite, that OpenAI should have made greater use of personal information by providing it to law enforcement eight months before the tragedy.

OpenAI now faces dozens of lawsuits in California filed by victims' family members and by the province of British Columbia. The B.C. government has already said it is pursuing legal options against OpenAI while several victims and their families have filed lawsuits against the tech firm. The Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner says OpenAI has filed for judicial review in B.C. Supreme Court, challenging the privacy office's request for certain documents as part of an ongoing investigation. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

stories.Headline: Amazon and Intel Tank the AI Trade. The 1 Factor Linking Big Tech’s Underwhelming Earnings.
stories.Summary:
On Friday, October 30, 2026, the Nasdaq fell to its lowest level in nearly three months after earnings from Amazon and Intel raised concerns about the cost of the AI buildout and when it will pay off. Amazon reported a sharp cash outflow in the third quarter and signaled another increase in capital expenditure next year, and its shares were down 2%. Intel said it would burn cash this year because of a weak PC market, manufacturing hurdles and heavy spending to expand production, and its shares were set for their steepest one-day drop on record, sliding almost 29%. The warning set off a selloff in chip stocks, with Nvidia down 3.7%, AMD down about 10% and the broader chips index down 7%, while server makers Dell and HP lost 10.4% and 8.7%.

Amazon and Intel were set to wipe out close to $200 billion in combined market value if losses held, and the Nasdaq-100 was set to erase just over $1 trillion that day and more than $2 trillion for the month. The S&P 500 information technology index was down 3.9%, its steepest one-day fall since June 23, and the communication services index was headed for its worst month since April 2022. Alphabet was down slightly after a record selloff the day before, when it reported a sharp rise in cash outflows, and a $6.3 billion record heist at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, also hurt appetite for crypto-linked and technology stocks, with Coinbase down 13%. At 11:52 a.m. ET the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 373.72 points, or 0.71%, at 51,968.84, the S&P 500 was down 120.20 points, or 1.56%, at 7,600.19, and the Nasdaq Composite was down 650.77 points, or 2.48%, at 25,533.95.

Joe Saluzzi, co-manager of trading at Themis Trading, said a lot of these companies got ahead of themselves, that it is all earnings based and right now they are not producing. He said that although Intel was having a terrible day, it is still up significantly this year, and the decline does not kill the whole story but is pretty much a reset. Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones, said the rotation into defensive sectors was supported by an above-trend pace of economic growth and by improving earnings growth from sectors that have lagged in recent years. Reddit plunged 28% after CEO Steve Huffman warned that total daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter.

Investors moved into consumer staples and healthcare, which were up 1.6% and 0.7% respectively, and healthcare hit a record high, while energy stocks were helped by gains of 1.7% in Chevron and 1.2% in Exxon Mobil after both beat third-quarter profit estimates. All three indexes were on course for weekly losses, and while the Dow was on track for monthly gains, the Nasdaq was set to snap a two-month winning streak in October. The Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates by more than 50 basis points by mid-2027, according to LSEG data, which could make debt-funded spending by companies harder to justify, and the central bank held rates this week as expected. Declining issues outnumbered advancers 1.71-to-1 on the NYSE and 2.85-to-1 on the Nasdaq, and the S&P 500 posted 42 new 52-week highs and five new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 60 new highs and 241 new lows.

stories.Headline: 60% of Youth Mentoring Professionals Are Using AI, but Most Lack Organizational Guidelines, New Research Finds
stories.Summary:
MENTOR released new research on October 29, 2026, finding that six in ten youth mentoring professionals surveyed already use generative artificial intelligence tools. The report is titled Human Connection in an AI World: The Opportunities and Challenges of Using AI in Delivering Youth Mentoring Services. It draws on interviews, a field survey, and stakeholder discussions. The findings show a growing disconnect between how quickly AI is entering youth-serving organizations and the policies, training, and resources available to help professionals use these tools responsibly.

Among those using AI, 84% use it to draft communications and grant materials, and 54% use it to manage notes and schedules. Far fewer report using AI for screening and matching at 15% or for direct youth engagement at 8%. While 67% of respondents expressed strategic interest in expanding AI use, only 8% reported having dedicated funding, leadership, or protocols to support implementation. Nearly three-quarters of respondents, 72%, identified professional development and staff training as needed supports, and 69% called for ethical guidelines.

Jermaine Myrie, CEO of MENTOR, said AI is already finding its way into mentoring programs, but too many organizations are being left to figure out how to use it responsibly on their own. He said there is an opportunity to change that by giving professionals the training, guidance, and support they need. He said human relationships built on trust, care, and connection are at the heart of this work. He said technology can strengthen that work, but relationships cannot be automated.

MENTOR supports the thoughtful use of AI in mentoring programs, including for administration, communications, fundraising, training, and data analysis. The organization also recognizes risks tied to data privacy, bias, and inaccurate information. It advocates for clear safeguards and human oversight as AI adoption expands. MENTOR hosted a webinar on October 27 featuring researcher Dr. Manolya Tanyu and MENTOR's Michael Garringer to discuss the findings and their implications for the field, and the recording is available on the report landing page alongside the full report and additional resources.

stories.Headline: Schneider Electric, Nscale and Start Campus Bring the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint into a Live AI Factory Environment
stories.Summary:
Schneider Electric, AVEVA, Nscale and Start Campus announced on October 27, 2026 the successful pilot of an end-to-end digital twin built with the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, part of NVIDIA DSX Sim. The pilot is called the Immersive Twin and connects Schneider Electric, AVEVA and ETAP technology in one digital platform. It runs at Nscale's operations inside the SIN01 data center on the 1.2 GW SINES Data Campus in Portugal, which Start Campus developed. The campus is described as one of Europe's largest and most sustainable AI factories and will soon host more than 66,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs.

The Immersive Twin combines engineering and operational data with power and cooling simulations and workload requirements to give a unified view of data center performance. It lets teams test what-if scenarios across power, cooling and process behavior before changes are made on-site, which can validate design decisions, assess upgrade impacts, reduce procurement risk and link IT and OT data. Nscale expects faster time to token, greater token efficiency, enhanced operations, increased flexibility and reduced risk when updating its technology stack. The pilot builds on earlier work in which Schneider Electric, AVEVA and ETAP joined the Alliance for OpenUSD last year to speed digital twin and AI factory development through the blueprint.

David Power, Chief Technology Officer at Nscale, said the companies are using digital twins to model how AI data centers operate in the real world, from power and cooling to token delivery, giving a clearer view of where full-stack optimizations can be realized before changes are made on the ground. Pankaj Sharma, Executive Vice President, Software & Service with Schneider Electric, said a credible end-to-end digital twin requires collaboration across the AI ecosystem and that connecting Nscale's workload and IT requirements with Start Campus's facility data helps model AI factories more holistically. Robert Dunn, Chief Executive Officer at Start Campus, said AI infrastructure needs to evolve as quickly as the technology it supports and that operators and customers work best from the same model. He said simulating how a jump in rack density moves through the power train and liquid cooling loop lets the companies test new hardware generations, agree the configuration with the customer and build it once.

The SINES Data Campus uses 100% renewable energy and targets a PUE of 1.1 and a WUE of 0 by harnessing the cooling power of the ocean. Start Campus provides the real-world infrastructure, engineering expertise and operational environment for the pilot, while Schneider Electric has 160,000 employees and 1 million partners in over 100 countries. The companies said the pilot supports the full lifecycle of AI factories, from design through operations, and advances interoperability through simulation-ready asset files. The articles do not say what further steps or timelines follow the pilot.

stories.Headline: K-water, Austin Sign AI Water MOU
stories.Summary:
K-water signed a memorandum of understanding with the City of Austin, Texas, on Oct. 29 at K-water's Han River Basin Headquarters in Gwacheon, Gyeonggi Province. The agreement was signed with a delegation led by Austin Deputy Mayor Michael Rogers. The deal covers cooperation on artificial intelligence-based smart water management. The agreement followed discussions that began in January this year at CES 2026, when the Austin Asian Chamber of Commerce showed interest in K-water's technological capabilities. The two sides continued exchanges, including the Korea-Texas Business Summit in August.

Under the agreement, the two organizations will cooperate on data-based water resources management and smart water management. Key areas include sharing best practices in water management and technology exchanges, holding joint seminars for capacity building, and identifying joint proof-of-concept projects for local application. Austin is known as Silicon Hills, where global companies including Samsung Electronics and Tesla are concentrated. Water demand there has recently surged due to urban development and the expansion of data centers, and Austin Water has been pursuing alternative water resources and smart technologies for a stable water supply. K-water plans to connect Austin's demand with its own digital capabilities to widen the basis for cooperation in the U.S. market.

Yoon Seog-dae, President of K-water, said the corporation will support efficient management of water resources in Austin based on water management capabilities accumulated over the past 60 years. He also said K-water plans to continuously expand the scope of cooperation so that Korean water companies can advance into the global market. The cooperation is expected to go beyond a simple technology exchange and lead to a broader expansion of the domestic water industry ecosystem. K-water also plans to support Korean water companies so they can demonstrate their technologies locally and seize business opportunities.

Separately, Marwynn Holdings, Inc. announced on Oct. 28 that it had entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding with Grenada National Resort. The MOU covers evaluation of the NexaCore AI & Renewable Energy Infrastructure Campus, a proposed solar power plant and AI data center on land within or associated with the Resort in Grenada. Marwynn's wholly-owned subsidiary, NexaCore Technologies, Inc., will lead project development, technology implementation, and day-to-day execution under Marwynn's oversight. The MOU sets an indicative project scale of approximately US$500 million, subject to feasibility, financing, approvals, and definitive agreements. NexaCore was formed in April 2026 to develop AI computing infrastructure and technical services.

The MOU gives NexaCore a specific site and a land partner to evaluate, and it gives 24 months of exclusivity, unless extended or superseded by definitive agreements. Either party may terminate on 30 days' written notice, and Marwynn may terminate immediately if it determines the project is not commercially or technically feasible. The proposed campus would pair on-site solar generation and battery storage with GPU-based computing capacity, with the solar plant intended to supply the data center's power needs and, where commercially viable, sell surplus energy. Ms. Yin Yan, CEO of Marwynn Holdings, said power supply is the hardest constraint in AI infrastructure, and that the MOU gives the company 24 months of exclusivity to test the model through land, grid, and connectivity studies before committing capital. She also said Grenada is the first site where the company can put that plan to work, with the campus to be developed in phases sized according to feasibility studies and financing support.

stories.Headline: SAP and NTT to Cooperate on Delivering Trusted Sovereign Cloud and SAP Business AI Capabilities - Engineering / Artificial Intelligence - SAP | KXEN
stories.Summary:
SAP SE and NTT, Inc. announced on October 29, 2026, in Tokyo, that they intend to cooperate on SAP Sovereign Cloud and SAP Business AI. The planned collaboration would combine SAP's enterprise applications, sovereign cloud and business AI with NTT's global infrastructure, integrated operations and industry AI expertise. The companies said the aim is to help customers use cloud and AI innovation while keeping control over sensitive data, operations, technology and security. The announcement reflects what the companies described as a shared ambition to advance secure, resilient and sovereign digital transformation for regulated industries.

As an initial area of cooperation, the companies plan to offer sovereign capabilities that pair the SAP Sovereign Cloud On-Site offering with NTT-managed infrastructure and operations in key markets. SAP Sovereign Cloud On-Site lets SAP-managed cloud solutions run in a customer-owned or customer-selected data center, giving local physical control, data residency and operational assurance. The companies intend to support customers in places where strong local control is required, including governments, defense organizations, defense industry companies, critical infrastructure operators and other regulated enterprises. They also intend to explore broader opportunities for those customers to modernize mission-critical processes and adopt AI in a secure, responsible and sovereign manner.

Dominik Asam, a member of the Executive Board and Chief Financial Officer of SAP SE, said the cooperation aims to give customers a practical path to cloud and AI innovation while keeping the control, governance and trust they need. He said sovereignty is not just a compliance requirement for public sector organizations and regulated industries but the foundation for resilience, competitiveness and responsible AI adoption. Yutaka Sasaki, Representative Member of the Board, Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NTT, said customers want practical ways to use AI to solve real business challenges and create new value. He said combining SAP's business applications and AI capabilities with NTT's understanding of industry needs and mission-critical operations aims to help organizations transform how they work and accelerate business outcomes.

The release describes the cooperation as a plan and intention rather than a completed agreement, and it includes forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. It says such statements are based on current expectations, forecasts and assumptions that could cause actual results to differ materially. It points to SAP's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including the risk factors section of SAP's 2025 Annual Report on Form 20-F, for more information on those risks. The release does not say what happens next beyond the planned initial cooperation and the intended exploration of broader opportunities.

stories.Headline: Why Is Nebius Group (NBIS) Expanding Its AI Infrastructure Reach?
stories.Summary:
Nebius Group N.V. extended its AI cloud reach and its shares rose 11.05 percent on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, according to Timothy Sykes coverage updated that day. The move followed upbeat coverage of its AI-driven cloud expansion, including a long-term 50-MW AIB data center deal that anchors its U.S. AI capacity. The stock opened near $159 and closed around $170.13, with an intraday high of $170.93, after running from the low $230s down into the $150s and bouncing back above $170 between October 2 and October 27, 2026. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang flagged Nebius as a high-demand neocloud while warning about working-capital and European power constraints.

The 50-MW commitment at AIB's southeastern U.S. data center runs under a 12-year agreement. Nebius also secured a $3.5B 364-day senior secured facility tied to Term SOFR plus 2.75 to 3.50 percent, aimed at building more data centers, buying GPUs and funding general needs. The Inferize acquisition adds infrastructure software that shortens time-to-launch and scaling for large AI models, and Nebius published live GPU spot prices, launched reserve auctions and pay-as-you-go pricing, and set up a program to return idle GPUs for credits. It is also running NVIDIA's simulation and training stack for Sereact's Cortex on its Physical AI Workbench in EU data centers, and an expanded EU AI builder program is backed by $10M in compute grants. Revenue is about $529.8M against an enterprise value near $41.68B, a price-to-sales ratio around 9,546 and price-to-book over 1,100, with negative return on assets and negative return on equity.

Huang called Nebius a neocloud with extremely strong AI demand and in the same breath warned about limited working capital and underbuilt European energy and infrastructure. The articles describe the stock as a momentum vehicle tied to real AI infrastructure growth but amplified by meme-style attention and short-dated financing risk, with multiple 1.8 to 2.8 percent premarket rebounds after 7 percent-plus drops often tied mainly to WallStreetBets and other retail-chatroom chatter. Tim Sykes said the market does not care about your opinion, it cares about price action, and advised studying catalysts, trading the pattern and always cutting losses quickly. The coverage states it is stock news, not investment advice.

Separately, Schneider Electric, industrial software provider AVEVA, AI cloud infrastructure company Nscale and data center developer Start Campus completed a pilot deployment of an end-to-end digital twin using the NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint, Yahoo Finance reported on Tuesday, October 27, 2026. The project, known as the Immersive Twin, is being implemented within Nscale's operations at the SIN01 data center at the SINES Data Campus in Portugal. The technology combines engineering information, operational data, power and cooling simulations and AI workload requirements to create a virtual representation of data center infrastructure. The companies said the pilot is intended to help operators assess infrastructure configurations, evaluate proposed changes and identify opportunities to improve computing efficiency before modification.

stories.Headline: UAE AI Office launches nationwide 'Vibe Coding' experience with Microsoft
stories.Summary:
The Artificial Intelligence Office in the UAE launched UAE Vibe Codes as part of UAE Codes Day, which is celebrated every year on 29 October. This year the event was held under the theme “Vibe Coding”. The office developed the initiative in collaboration with Microsoft. It attracted 5,000 participants within its first hour of launch.

The initiative lets people turn ideas into websites and digital applications using artificial intelligence in just minutes, with no prior programming experience needed. It can be accessed at https://uaecodesday.specnt.com, where participants describe their ideas in natural language and AI-powered tools help turn them into working prototypes. The invitation is open to everyone in the UAE regardless of age, background or field of expertise, including students, educators, entrepreneurs, business owners and government and private sector employees. Participants can build things such as a website to address a workplace challenge, an application to organise daily tasks, a digital tool to support a startup or an educational solution.

Omar Sultan Al Olama, Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, said the UAE continues to build a national model for empowering society with the tools of the future. He said the true value of artificial intelligence lies in expanding human innovation and unlocking new ways to turn ideas into reality. He noted that the initiative aims to strengthen people’s confidence in their ability to innovate and create solutions that respond to society’s needs. He added that UAE Codes Day is a national opportunity to broaden public participation in shaping the digital future, and that what once seemed beyond reach is now within everyone’s grasp.

UAE Codes Day sees participation from government entities, private sector organisations and entrepreneurs, including the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Justice, the General Authority of Islamic Affairs, Endowments and Zakat, the UAE Space Agency, Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority, Etisalat UAE, du, Emirates Health Services, Emirates NBD and Furjan Dubai. The Office of Artificial Intelligence is organising hands-on workshops with partners including Google, Emirates Global Aluminium, Siemens and IBM. The office is also collaborating with Emaar and cinemas across the UAE to promote the experience through their digital screens and platforms. In October 2021, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum directed that 29 October be designated annually as UAE Codes Day, and in November 2023 UNESCO adopted the UAE’s proposal to designate 29 October as the International Day of Programming.

stories.Headline: artificial intelligence: Pope Leo warns AI agents are 'tools, not persons'
stories.Summary:
Pope Leo XIV warned on Friday, October 30, 2026, against granting artificial intelligence agents legal personhood or rights. He made the statement in a speech to leading international AI experts gathered at the Vatican for a dialogue on the technology's future. The pope said the responsibility for the actions of AI systems should lie firmly with their human creators. He told the gathering that machines are tools, not persons.

The pope said so-called artificial intelligences do not undergo experiences, do not possess a body, and do not feel joy or pain. He added that they do not mature through relationships and do not know from within what love, work, friendship or responsibility mean. He warned that some people today propose granting these systems rights or even legal personhood. Such an approach, he said, risks obscuring human responsibility and leaving those who suffer harm to confront a faceless entity.

Leo, who is 71, has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically. His first encyclical, published in May, called for putting the technology at the service of human dignity. He said the future of artificial intelligence is not pre-determined, and humans have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications. He said some decisions must never be delegated, and those affecting human life, freedom and the use of force must always remain subject to effective, informed and responsible human oversight.

The pope repeated his call for a ban on lethal autonomous weapons and said intelligent technologies must be directed toward the common good. He said there was an urgent need for shared standards, independent oversight and clear mechanisms of accountability. He added that it was key to ensure decisions concerning the development and use of AI can be examined, challenged when necessary, and accompanied by appropriate remedies for any harm caused. The debate over the risks of the technology has intensified in recent months, fuelled by several incidents of systems taking unauthorized actions and apocalyptic warnings from industry professionals.

stories.Summary:
Rob Illidge, a 40 year old CEO from Manchester, founded the LinkedIn employee advocacy software company Vulse in 2019 as a side project. After a year of development he secured funding and grew the business, reaching 14 employees within a couple of years. Starting in 2023, over a three year period, he made more than 64 per cent of his staff redundant, cutting his marketing, sales and development teams. In total he replaced nine employees with artificial intelligence, and graduates faced the greatest risk because the technology took over repetitive tasks.

The company now runs with a team of just five people, and Illidge says this saves more than £100,000 a year in staffing costs. He says the AI tools cost £140 a month, while employing one person on an average salary costs more than £500 a month in National Insurance and pension alone. Staffing every replaced role at former staff pay would cost around £250,000 a year, and revenue per employee rose 25 times in two years, from around £1,500 to over £38,000. Vulse was valued at £750,000 in 2023 and its most recent valuation puts it at £5m, with monthly recurring revenue up 76 per cent year on year.

Illidge said the business would not be where it is today without AI, which he says does two to three times the work of an employee and keeps working overnight. He said staff costs put a lot of pressure on businesses and the money was better spent elsewhere, adding that AI could do a better job. He described being a founder as a balancing act, because you are responsible for livelihoods but also have a business to develop, and said he is becoming more comfortable with that. He called the redundancies a blessing in disguise and said those let go will find a better job.

Illidge said he agrees AI development should slow down, but that it is helping UK businesses like his. He said AI has levelled the playing field, with enquiries now coming from all over the world and not just the UK, and that he is looking to grow. He said most businesses should take advantage of AI, and that when he speaks at universities many students are studying AI topics. He said new roles are being created as a result of AI, which he called a positive because those are the jobs that will be available.

stories.Headline: artificial intelligence: Global trading is mixed as worries about AI-related issues grow
stories.Summary:
Global shares traded mixed on Friday, October 30, 2026, as worries about the future of artificial intelligence grew after a drop in Alphabet's stock dragged on U.S. markets. In early trading, France's CAC 40 gained 0.2% to 7,988.84, while Germany's DAX edged down 0.1% to 26,008.99 and Britain's FTSE 100 added nearly 0.4% to 10,759.33. U.S. shares were set to trade mixed, with Dow futures up 0.2% at 52,613.00 and S&P 500 futures down 0.8% at 7,689.00. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 2.1% to finish at 63,290.11, South Korea's Kospi declined 3.5% to 5,730.74 as shares in SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics slipped, and the Shanghai Composite lost 1.4% to 3,599.02. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.2% to 8,908.10, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng added 1.5% to 23,294.42.

At the end of its two-day monetary policy board meeting, the Bank of Japan kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 1.25%, which was widely expected because the central bank raised the rate last month. The U.S. has been pressuring Japan to raise rates because of concerns about the weakening yen. In currency trading, the U.S. dollar fell to 157.28 Japanese yen from 157.65 yen, and the euro cost $1.1196, up from $1.1181. On Wall Street, the S&P 500 fell 0.3% for its first loss in four days, the Nasdaq composite tumbled 1.4%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 132 points, or 0.3%. Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% for their worst day since they began trading more than 20 years ago.

All told, the S&P 500 fell 23.59 points to 7,720.39 on Thursday, the Dow dropped 132.54 to 52,342.56, and the Nasdaq tumbled 365.13 to 26,184.72. The yield on the 10-year Treasury fell to 4.94% from 5.05% late Wednesday. AI-related stocks have been volatile, with shares of chipmakers and other companies rising on enthusiasm for the technology and then falling on concerns such as supply constraints. In energy trading, benchmark U.S. crude gained 1.53% to $103.56 a barrel, and Brent crude edged up 1.65% to $116.77 a barrel. The articles do not say what happens next beyond these market moves.

Celestica reported third quarter results on Oct. 26, 2026, and its shares rose 12% after the report. The Canadian contract electronics manufacturer said revenue grew 83% year over year to $5.83 billion, while adjusted earnings more than doubled to $3.30 per share. Its connectivity and cloud solutions segment produced 84% of revenue and grew 102%, with networking up 68% to $3.26 billion and compute and storage up 242% to $1.61 billion. The company's customers include Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, and Intel.

Celestica raised its 2026 guidance to a 69% revenue increase to $21 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $11.55, up 91%. It had originally expected $16 billion in revenue and $8.20 in adjusted earnings per share for 2026. For 2027, it expects $40 billion in revenue, a 90% jump, and adjusted earnings per share of $21.50, up 86%. SemiAnalysis predicts global data center capacity net additions could reach 51.2 gigawatts in 2027, more than double this year's 25 gigawatts.

Harsh Chauhan of The Motley Fool wrote that Celestica trades at 14 times forward earnings, the same multiple as Nvidia. He said Celestica's 2027 forecast puts it on track to grow faster than Nvidia, which expects 70% revenue growth next year. He wrote that at 21 times earnings at the end of 2028, based on projected earnings per share of $31.27, the stock could reach $660, implying 144% upside. He has no position in the stocks mentioned.

A second article by Adam Spatacco said the Shiller CAPE ratio stands around 41 against a historical average of about 17, and the Buffett indicator is around 230%, while Warren Buffett warns of danger near 200%. He wrote that Apple and Alphabet, both held by Berkshire Hathaway, could still thrive in a downturn. Apple's fiscal third quarter revenue was $109.4 billion, up 16%, with iPhone revenue up 22%, Mac sales up 30%, and Services revenue of $30.7 billion, up 12%. Alphabet's Gemini models are being integrated across Google Workspace and Android, and its Tensor Processing Units offer customers an alternative to Nvidia GPUs.

stories.Headline: AI in combat: When humans are in the loop, but not in control
stories.Summary:
In March 2026, Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, described how AI tools helped his personnel sort through large amounts of information during Operation Epic Fury against Iran, cutting task time from hours or days to seconds. He said humans will always make the final decisions on what to shoot, what not to shoot, and when to shoot. The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists published an article on October 30, 2026 arguing that the real question is not whether humans stay involved but whether their involvement is meaningful rather than nominal. The article gives the example of an operator authorizing a strike on a building, where a well-trained operator with a clear interface can weigh the evidence, while an untrained one under pressure keeps formal authority but has little real judgement.

The article says keeping humans in the loop is only a first step and must come with responsible procurement, training, and structures. It notes that NATO acquired Palantir's Maven Smart System in just six months, raising concern that the pressure to adopt such systems may weaken scrutiny. It cites the Ukrainian Saker Scout drone, which can recognize military equipment but cannot tell Ukrainian from Russian targets, and quotes Rostyslav Olenchyn of Twist Robotics warning that you should be sure there are no civilians and not your own people. It also cites Anna Rubinstein, formerly Chief of Responsible Artificial Intelligence at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and Director of Test and Evaluation for Project Maven, saying technology cannot just be dropped in someone's lap without training and tradecraft. It adds that former US Navy officer Emelia Probasco spent a month learning to operate the AEGIS Combat System, and more than five years after Maven's rollout its users lacked comparable preparation.

The article says militaries must test systems so personnel can scrutinize recommendations and understand their limits, and training should be continuous, covering incomplete information and possible manipulation. It says structures must give operators time and authority to exercise judgement, options to seek more information or refer decisions to a commander, and incentives that reward scrutiny. It warns that human review can become a bottleneck as AI produces recommendations at greater speed and scale, as reported by the Financial Times. It concludes that when an AI-assisted decision goes wrong, scrutiny must extend beyond the person who approved it to those who chose the system, set the pace of operations, and shaped the conditions of its use.

Separately, NTT DATA INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT CONSULTING, Inc., headquartered in Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo, with President and CEO Shigeki Yamaguchi, announced on October 29, 2026 the launch of SPARK, an AI-powered consulting service for knowledge workers in strategic business activities. Its first offering, AI Foresight & Intelligence, was available the same day, and two more are planned: AI-era Knowledge Management and Agentic AI Adoption Practice. The company says the service continuously identifies emerging developments through AI and feeds human judgment into a learning loop to assess impact on business opportunities and risks, with people deciding whether to accept, revise, or reject the resulting information. The company plans to roll out all three offerings in phases.

stories.Headline: Google expands AI Mode ads globally amid slowing Search growth
stories.Summary:
Google said on Wednesday, alongside Alphabet's third-quarter 2026 results, that it is expanding advertising in its AI Mode search experience to new markets for the first time. Ads in AI Mode are coming to Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore. Google plans to extend the rollout to Brazil, Mexico and the United Kingdom in the fourth quarter. In the US, it is also launching multi-turn ads that appear in follow-up queries within AI Mode, and the ads will carry a "Sponsored" label.

The expansion arrives as growth in the company's core search advertising business slows. Search and other advertising revenue rose 12 per cent year over year to $63.35 billion in the September quarter, down from 17 per cent in the second quarter and 19 per cent in the first. Alphabet's total revenue was $127.6 billion, up 25 per cent, slightly under analyst projections of $127.93 billion. Google Services brought in $96.3 billion, up 11 per cent, while Google Cloud revenue rose 103 per cent to $30.7 billion. Earnings per share came in at $2.12 against expectations of $2.99, a figure the company attributed to an unrealized loss on its SpaceX stake, and capital expenditure for the quarter reached $51.4 billion, mostly for AI infrastructure.

Philipp Schindler, Google's chief business officer, said the slowdown reflected foreign exchange rates and one-off ad spending dips in Asia-Pacific among advertisers hit by the EU's end of its de minimis exemption on low-cost imports. He also said strong growth in AI Mode queries weighed on search growth because the product earns less per query, and that tests of ads there have returned promising results. Click-through rates for sponsored and organic product listings in AI Mode are similar, he said, and Google's research suggests users find the ads relevant. CEO Sundar Pichai said AI investments are driving overall query growth, including commercial queries, with year-over-year query growth at its highest in five years. He added that AI Mode queries are on average three times longer than traditional searches and that one in five AI Mode searches globally involves voice, images or documents.

Alphabet shares fell between 8 per cent and roughly 11 per cent in after-hours trading, according to the reports. The company left its 2026 capital expenditure outlook unchanged at $195 billion to $205 billion, and finance chief Anat Ashkenazi said spending is still expected to increase significantly in 2027. Google also said it has secured $561 billion in future cloud revenue from customer contracts, and it has begun renting computing capacity from third-party providers, which Ashkenazi said will pressure margins in the short term. Schindler said Google plans to scale ads across both AI Mode and AI Overviews to more users and queries, and is confident it can build advertising models for agentic uses. Some publishers, meanwhile, are objecting to Google's use of one crawler for both search indexing and AI, and no publisher traffic figures were mentioned on this call.

stories.Headline: DeepSeek, Moonshot AI used OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra for training models
stories.Summary:
Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model to train their latest systems, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter. The practice is known as distillation, in which one model is improved by using the answers of a more capable model as training data. The report said Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro, released last week, and DeepSeek's upgraded V4.1-Flash 1017, launched on October 17, both benefited from distilling Astra. OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

Kimi K3.1 Pro is an upgrade of Kimi K3, which came out in July, and was developed through post-training. It uses a mixture-of-experts design with 2.8 trillion total parameters and 104 billion active parameters, selecting 16 of its 896 experts as it processes each token. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it scored 55, ranking fourth and ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 53, while its predecessor scored 44. It also took first place on Terminal Bench 4.0 with 67 percent, up from 13 percent for Kimi K3 and ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 64 percent. The model costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, and Artificial Analysis put its average cost at $2.11 per task, against $5.98 for Claude Opus 5.5 at maximum reasoning effort.

On responsibility, OpenAI said in a September 30 blog post that it had tied a core part of a distillation campaign, which began in July, to individuals associated with Moonshot AI. Separately, the US government, Anthropic and OpenAI have accused Moonshot AI of unauthorized distillation of their models. Anthropic alleged that Moonshot used fraudulent accounts and proxy networks to gather responses and reasoning traces from its Claude models and used them to train Kimi. Moonshot AI and DeepSeek had not responded to the claims at the time of reporting.

The dispute comes as US-China technology competition intensifies, and leading US firms, including Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, argue that distillation lets rivals reproduce advanced capabilities more quickly and at lower cost. Earlier this month, Anthropic said new measures to stop copying of its Claude models had cut the data harvested in distillation attacks by roughly 90 to 99 percent. Artificial Analysis noted that Kimi K3.1 Pro offers top-tier performance at a reasonable price, but runs slower than average at 73 tokens per second against 81, and produces very long responses, using 150 million tokens in its evaluation against a median of 87 million. The articles do not say what steps may follow.

stories.Headline: AI is tearing up decades of computer science research.
stories.Summary:
OpenAI claimed on Monday that its AI had disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a 27-year-old assumption about how the effort to solve certain problems grows with their size. The company said the disproof was produced on October 16 and formalised in Lean, a tool that checks proofs against formal rules, the next day. Anthropic also claimed this week to have disproved the hypothesis. OpenAI published the explanation and formal proof on GitHub, and the claims have not been independently verified.

The hypothesis held that the time needed to solve certain problems increases exponentially as they grow larger, and much theoretical computer science on complexity and algorithm design was built on that premise. The result, if confirmed, would make around 50 of UC Santa Barbara professor Daniel Lokshtanov's published papers either pointless or in need of a revisit. Linköping University professor Peter Jonsson said much of his work, due to be presented in two weeks at the IEEE Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science, is now dead. Thore Husfeldt, head of the algorithms research group at the IT University of Copenhagen, said the problem he had spent most of this year on is now all irrelevant.

OpenAI asked the UC Santa Barbara computer scientists who originally proposed the hypothesis, plus an MIT academic who has refuted a version of it, to rally researchers to unpack the proofs. The effort so far includes a Google form asking for volunteers and feedback, and a commitment from OpenAI to fund a conference on the topic. OpenAI also convened computer scientists Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams to lead a group examining the result. Lokshtanov plans to join the effort, and Jonsson plans to revisit his own and others' papers that depend on the hypothesis being true.

Husfeldt said the finding is fantastic and described it as like somebody illuminating an entire subfield in floodlights. He said the last few months have been tough and that his department has considered hiring an occupational psychologist because some people are really depressed. Victor Lagerkvist, an associate professor at Linköping, plans to return to problems he had given up on under the assumption the hypothesis was accurate. Lokshtanov said the result does not directly affect cryptography but should definitely scare some cryptosystem designers.

stories.Headline: Oracle expands chip supply deal with Nvidia, adds Google and Cerebras offerings
stories.Summary:
Oracle said on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at its Oracle AI World event in Las Vegas that it is expanding its cloud AI chip arrangement with Nvidia while also adding chips from other suppliers, including Google and Cerebras Systems. The company says the goal is to give customers more choice for running different kinds of artificial intelligence workloads. Oracle will become the first hyperscaler to offer Google's Tensor Processing Units outside Google Cloud, and it also plans to deploy inference chips from OpenAI, SambaNova Systems and Positron AI. The announcement came alongside news that Google Cloud and Oracle are widening their partnership across the AI stack.

On the Nvidia side, Oracle said Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs are now generally available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and that it will grow its OCI Superclusters to multi-gigawatt scale using the Vera Rubin systems. Customers can scale CPU and GPU resources independently, which is meant to cut idle capacity and raise utilisation. Google TPUs for training and inference are due on OCI in 2027, with adoption ramping over several years, and the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine is also set for 2027. Positron AI's Positron Atlas inference chip is already generally available. Oracle will also use its own Acceleron networking chips in some Nvidia-based systems in place of certain Nvidia networking chips.

Mahesh Thiagarajan, president of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, said different AI workloads have different compute needs, and that this choice lets customers pick the right infrastructure for the performance, throughput and economics of each one. Andrew Feldman, chief executive of Cerebras, called the deal a massive expansion of his company's base of tier-one customers. Analyst Brendan Burke of Futurum Group said the move fits an industry shift toward mixed computing, while Matt Kimball of Moor Insights & Strategy described it as Oracle trying to be the open silicon cloud. Burke added that Oracle must show the new accelerators can compete with Nvidia-based offerings and that it is committed to them for the long term.

Oracle's cloud has relied mainly on Nvidia GPUs, though analysts say it also runs some AMD GPUs. Nvidia leads the market for chips that train AI systems, but inference has a wider field of competitors. Google's latest TPU family includes the TPU 8t for training and the TPU 8i for inference, which Google says deliver up to twice the performance per watt of the prior generation. OpenAI and Broadcom have said they expect the first Jalapeño inference accelerators by the end of 2026, but Oracle gave no date for them on OCI, and SambaNova's SN50 chips also have no stated availability.

stories.Headline: Put ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini to work for $79
stories.Summary:
A campaign tracked as Yoba was discovered by Check Point Research, which published its findings on October 27, 2026. The attackers created fake GitHub projects pretending to be desktop applications called GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus. The first repository was created around July 2026, but the first two malicious releases were not uploaded until the end of August 2026, and a third followed about five days later. The malware was placed next to legitimate, signed executables from OpenAI and Anthropic so it could be loaded indirectly, a technique known as DLL sideloading.

The campaign used three repositories, each with a different email address, and the uploaders appeared to operate in different time zones, which the report says was likely a deliberate attempt to hide the actor's true location. The releases were named sol-setup.zip, Setup-Claude.zip, and GPT-6-Astra-Setup.zip. The malicious component was a file called winmm.dll, which was compiled on August 30, 2026, the same day it was added to the ZIP archive. The installers contained a malicious component called YobaDropper, which included another component called YobaLoader that contacted attacker-controlled infrastructure and fetched the final payload. The attackers avoided dedicated command-and-control infrastructure and instead relied on Telegram, Tor, Catbox, and DNS over HTTPS.

The report says the actor behind the campaign shows indicators suggesting Russian origins and appears to operate primarily in the UTC-4 time zone. The repositories did not show fake stars or forks, but they still appeared among the top results on Google, most likely due to SEO poisoning, where the attackers optimized titles, descriptions, and hosting domains. The report describes the campaign as demonstrating strong operational security. The malicious ZIP files were not password-protected, because the binaries already had very low detection rates thanks to anti-sandbox and other anti-analysis techniques.

The fake projects used real GitHub infrastructure and GitHub.io pages describing the software's capabilities, with download links pointing to the malicious releases hosted on GitHub. The report says the website showed search-targeted content and suspicious installer-delivery tactics consistent with an SEO-poisoning lure. stories.Headline: Microsoft offers quarter of global workforce voluntary buyouts as AI spending accelerates
stories.Summary:
Microsoft has offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly 27% of its global workforce, as it pours money into artificial intelligence. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer in a blog post on Monday, October 26, 2026. The offer was open to eligible employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States. Microsoft had about 223,000 full-time employees at the end of June.

According to Computing UK, the programme covers employees at vice-president level and below in selected teams, and staff will be told by email with a link to the details. The terms are expected to resemble Microsoft's standard severance arrangements. Bloomberg reported that the teams involved include Windows, Copilot, Xbox and Finance, while some groups, including employees working in datacentres, sales and marketing, are excluded. It is not yet clear how many people will accept, and Microsoft has not said how much it expects to save or whether more workforce changes are planned.

Coleman said the offer is meant to give employees more flexibility and control over their future careers, and described it as something new for the company that it will learn from. She added that Microsoft will keep helping people concentrate on the most important work, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find other opportunities inside the company. Computing UK noted that the programme builds on lessons from an earlier voluntary retirement initiative. More than 30% of the roughly 8,750 workers eligible for that earlier offer accepted it.

The move comes as spending on AI data centers is expected to top $700 billion this year across the industry, which has made memory chips, processors, other equipment and electricity more expensive. Economists expect that to keep pushing up inflation at least through the end of this year. CBS News, as cited by Mashable, reported that Microsoft itself is expected to spend $175 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026. In July, the company said it was cutting 4,800 jobs, about 2.1% of its global workforce, including many in its Xbox video game business. Microsoft's stock hit an all-time high this month and rose about 1% on Monday, and the company is due to report quarterly financial results on Wednesday.

stories.Headline: AI chips worth $15.5 million seized at Malaysia airport, Customs authority says
stories.Summary:
Malaysian customs announced on Oct 28 that it had seized advanced artificial intelligence chips worth about RM49.5 million this month, which converts to roughly S$15.5 million or US$12.1 million. The haul came on Oct 15, when officers inspecting the free trade zone at Kuala Lumpur International Airport found 30 server units containing the chips. Authorities say they are closing in on a syndicate suspected of smuggling high-performance semiconductors through Malaysia's main airport. The shipment is said to have come from an Asian country and was due to be sent on to another country in the same continent.

That onward movement was a re-export, which required a trade permit, according to the initial findings of the investigation. Customs officials said the servers had been falsely declared as electronic components. The aim, they said, was to move the goods through Malaysia so that no restrictions would apply when they were exported to the next destination. A Malaysian firm that helped arrange the shipment has been called in to assist with the investigation.

The details were given to reporters by Aspalila Ag Tuah, the customs director at Kuala Lumpur International Airport. She said the October shipment is suspected to be the work of the same network behind a similar smuggling attempt that customs foiled in June. According to her, at least five cases are tied to the syndicate, and together they involve seizures of chips worth more than RM100 million. She declined to give more details, saying the probe is still under way.

The case sits against the backdrop of export controls that Malaysia put in place in 2025 on the movement of advanced AI chips of US origin. Malaysia took that step after pressure from the United States to stem the flow of such chips into China. Reports on the seizure also pointed to a separate US case, in which a man was arrested over the alleged smuggling of US$300 million worth of computer servers to China. Authorities in Malaysia have not said when the investigation into the syndicate will conclude, and no charges were mentioned in the reports.

stories.Headline: Opportunities in China's AI undervalued
stories.Summary:
ManageEngine, an India-based division of Zoho Corporation that provides enterprise IT management solutions, recently released Zia AI agents across its full-stack IT management products for the Chinese market. It launched more than 30 AI agents in the first batch and plans to raise the number to over 100 by the end of 2026. The company has been in China for about 20 years and has served over 5,000 enterprises there, with partnerships with more than 100 organizations. Mathivanan Venkatachalam, the firm's global vice president, visited Beijing and was scheduled to meet a customer in Shenzhen on Wednesday.

During the visit, ManageEngine announced it will invest 425 million yuan, or 63.73 million dollars, in the Chinese market over the next five years. The funds will mainly go to data center construction, AI research and development, technical support systems and its partner ecosystem. Venkatachalam said overseas platforms such as Google do not suit domestic needs, so the company engaged with China's large-model ecosystem and integrated its products with local models such as DeepSeek. He said the firm has invested in localization research over the past five or six years. Other Indian firms are also using Chinese open-weight models such as DeepSeek and Kimi to cut costs, and India launched the IndiaAI Mission in March 2024 to give AI startups access to GPU computing resources and policy and financial support.

Venkatachalam said the localization work over recent years was an important reason for the continued investment. Mansoor Nadeem Lari, CEO of Silk Route Trade and Industry Development Corp, said his organization is exploring cooperation with global AI models for e-commerce and had been in touch with Accio Work, an Alibaba platform, and expected to cooperate with China's e-commerce AI ecosystem soon. Xiang Ligang, president of the Beijing Institute of Intelligent Era Industry, said India's large population and diverse languages give it rich data for training models. Qian Feng of Tsinghua University's National Strategy Institute said the two countries have complementary strengths and can deepen cooperation in research, market expansion and standards-setting.

The article cites a Goldman Sachs report, reported by ANI on October 21, saying India's listed AI market could gain 50 billion to 100 billion dollars in market capitalization over the next two to five years as private AI companies move toward IPOs. It also cites Reuters reporting that Tata Communications announced investments of close to 450 million dollars on Monday to build high-speed network cables linking India's AI data-center corridors. Manish Bhandari of Vallum Capital Advisors said India had empaneled 18,693 GPUs, including 12,896 H100s, as of early 2025, with plans to roughly double that. He said realistic cooperation looks like arm's-length absorption of open models rather than joint compute or data-sharing ventures.

stories.Headline: HBM explained: the AI memory behind SK Hynix’s record profits and rising chip prices
stories.Summary:
SK Hynix reported record third-quarter results on Oct. 29, 2026, with revenue of 104.6155 trillion won and operating profit of 83.3338 trillion won, the first 100 trillion won quarter in company history. Revenue rose 327.9% and operating profit 632.1% from a year earlier, and the operating margin reached 79.7%. The company has now set all-time highs for six consecutive quarters. The results beat securities industry estimates by 6.5% and 8.3%, respectively.

The company said DRAM and HBM volumes are effectively sold out through 2029. SK Hynix has signed long-term supply agreements with 14 customers, including major global cloud service providers, and contracted volumes cover more than 50% of total production capacity for 2027 and 2028. On Oct. 29, Yuanta Securities raised its price target to 3.7 million won from 3.3 million won and projected fourth-quarter revenue of 147.1 trillion won and operating profit of 118.2 trillion won. Shinhan Securities lifted its target to 3 million won and forecast fourth-quarter revenue of 126.1 trillion won and operating profit of 101.5 trillion won. HBM4 is expected to surpass HBM3E in shipment volume and revenue share in the fourth quarter, and expanded operations at the M15X plant in Cheongju will lift fourth-quarter DRAM shipments by more than 20% from the prior quarter.

Park Jun-deok, vice president of DRAM marketing, said DRAM and HBM volumes are effectively all sold out through 2029, dismissing peak-out concerns. Kwak Noh-jung, president of SK Hynix, said customer trust built on technological competitiveness has translated into long-term contracts, improving visibility on medium- to long-term profitability. Chief Financial Officer Kim Woo-hyun said volumes secured through long-term agreements account for more than 50% of production capacity for 2027 and 2028 and forecast that the supply shortage would persist through 2030. Yuanta analyst Baek Gil-hyun said earnings visibility is far higher than in past semiconductor cycles, and Shinhan analyst Kim Hyung-tae noted the 12-month forward price-to-book ratio is 1.7 times, the cheapest valuation among DRAM peers.

SK Hynix shares rose as high as 1.536 million won on the morning of Oct. 29, up 3.30% from the previous session, after a 10.89% gain the prior day. The KOSPI closed at 6,012.44 on the 28th, up 6.63%, retaking the 6,000 level for the first time in 10 trading sessions. SK Hynix plans to buy about 20 trillion won of its own shares on the open market from the 29th through Jan. 28 next year, part of a shareholder return plan totaling 100 trillion won this year that includes more than 30 trillion won in cash dividends and additional buybacks on top of 40 trillion won in treasury share cancellations. Customer requests for HBM exceed twice the level the company can supply, and analysts expect profit growth to continue as long as supply expansion centered on high-value products continues in an environment of limited capacity additions.

stories.Headline: CoreWeave Stocks Rebound 5.6% as AI Financing Faces Scrutiny
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave's stock bounced back sharply this week after a rough stretch for AI infrastructure companies. Shares rose about 6.8% to $58.95 around midday on October 27, the day the company said it had brought most of a new Copenhagen data center online. On Tuesday, the stock climbed almost 8%, gaining $4.38 to close at $59.57, while the Nasdaq-100 rose just over 1%. Other neocloud and AI infrastructure names also advanced as investors rotated back into the sector.

The Copenhagen site, its first deployment in Denmark, is operated by atNorth and is designed to provide 22.5 megawatts of IT capacity. It runs NVIDIA Blackwell systems linked by Quantum-X800 InfiniBand networking, and it brings CoreWeave's European footprint to nine data centers across five markets, including the U.K., Spain, Sweden and Norway. CoreWeave also plans to extend its network into the United Arab Emirates, India, Indonesia, Singapore, Australia, South Korea and Japan, with rollout starting in late 2026 and a network spanning four continents targeted for mid-2027. As of June 30, the company operated 51 data centers with more than 1.5 gigawatts of active power, and it reported about 4.2 gigawatts of contracted power on its Aug. 11 earnings call.

The rebound followed weeks of pressure over how heavily indebted AI infrastructure firms can keep financing their expansion. CoreWeave lost roughly a quarter of its value in one recent week amid worries about its debt load of about $50 billion and higher borrowing costs. A GuruFocus analyst described the rally as a recovery in sentiment rather than proof that the financing problem is solved, and said the company must show its balance sheet can support demand. A separate GuruFocus piece noted that CoreWeave is loss-making, with a market value of $32.51 billion, an enterprise value of $77.71 billion and a GF Score of 15 out of 100. It also pointed out that the Denmark announcement brought no new contracted revenue and no utilization figure for the site.

Tuesday's lift came as Anthropic's IPO filing showed strong demand for computing power, with $16.3 billion in first-half revenue, nearly 14 times the year-earlier figure, along with large long-term compute commitments. Tech Contrarians' Sara Awad, speaking on an Investing Experts podcast published Tuesday, took a more cautious view. She expects a potential bubble burst in 2027 driven more by funding pressure than weak demand, and she favors chip equipment and optical-networking firms such as ASML over capital-intensive operators like CoreWeave, IREN and Hut 8. She said CoreWeave has fallen more than 50% from its highs. Analysts say investors will watch bond yields, funding costs, new capacity, backlog conversion and whether revenue growth turns into stronger free cash flow.

stories.Headline: MPs call for ban on generative AI in primary schools
stories.Summary:
On Thursday, 29 October 2026, members of the Dutch Tweede Kamer, the lower house of parliament, backed a motion calling on the government to ban primary school pupils from using generative AI. The motion was proposed by Volt and the CDA and submitted by Volt leader Laurens Dassen during a debate on the education budget. It was also signed by lawmakers from PRO, D66, the Partij voor de Dieren, DENK, 50PLUS, the SP, the ChristenUnie and JA21. According to broadcaster NOS, the motion has the backing of 10 parties holding 88 of the 150 seats.

The motion asks the cabinet to arrange a formal rule disallowing tools such as ChatGPT for primary school pupils. It argues that young pupils develop critical thinking, creativity and imagination largely in primary school, and that generative AI poses a risk to this development. The ban would not stop schools from teaching pupils about AI, even if children themselves were not allowed to use it. New statutory curriculum guidelines say pupils should learn to interact responsibly with an AI system and to identify and describe artificial intelligence. According to DutchNews, new learning goals due to take effect in 2027 will require pupils to explore AI, and secondary school students will start experimenting with training AI systems.

Dassen said he believes in the opportunities AI offers but that generative AI is widening learning gaps. He said the Netherlands must not make the same mistake it made when social media was embraced uncritically, and that pupils should learn to read, write and do arithmetic before using AI. CDA parliamentarian Etkin Armut said generative AI has no place in primary school pupils' learning and that learning from books should remain the foundation. The PO-Raad, the umbrella organization for Dutch primary education, said it understood lawmakers' concerns but was taken aback by the majority backing a complete ban, which a spokesperson said came out of the blue.

The PO-Raad noted that research suggests frequent use of generative AI by pupils appears to reduce learning outcomes. It said it is extremely important that pupils learn to analyze a source and think critically for themselves, and that children also encounter AI outside the classroom, so teachers should be able to make pupils aware of the pitfalls. It also pointed to possible benefits of AI tools designed for educational purposes. The organization wants to work with the Education Ministry and experts to agree on how generative AI should be handled in primary education, saying something clearly needs to be done. Education specialist Barend Last, who teaches the final year of primary school, told NOS he agreed children should not have unlimited access to AI, but said it can be a useful teaching tool if used in the right way, and that ruling it out altogether risks children learning too little about it.
